title: Squid denies a request because the domain is not in the allowlist
symptoms: 403 Forbidden returned by the proxy for an outbound request
curl: (56) Received HTTP code 403 from proxy after CONNECT
Invalid domain "<entry>": ports are not supported / URL paths and queries are not supported / unsupported scheme (AWF rejects the allowlist entry before startup)
conditions: The destination host resolves but Squid logs TCP_DENIED:HIER_NONE for it
The domain (or its parent domain) is absent from --allow-domains / network.allowDomains

An allowlist entry written as host:port, a URL path, user@host, or a non-HTTP(S) scheme is rejected with an actionable error on current main; AWF builds before #11952 could instead normalize such entries into a non-matching Squid ACL and surface only as a 403 (affected release range unknown)
http:// and https:// prefixes are recognized case-insensitively on current main and keep their protocol-specific ACL; a single trailing slash is accepted
rootCause: Egress filtering is working as designed: the requested domain is not covered by the generated Squid domain ACL.

probe.command: docker exec awf-squid awk '/TCP_DENIED/ { print $1, $2, $3, $7, $8 }' /var/log/squid/access.log | tail -20
probe.expect: Shows timestamp, client, host, status, and decision for denied traffic; the host is absent from the allowlist.

action: Add the specific required domain (not a broad wildcard) to the allowlist after confirming it is expected traffic. Keep egress filtering on; if the denial looks like exfiltration, route to SEC-001. If AWF rejects an entry, use a bare domain or wildcard (optionally http:// or https://) without a port; use --allow-urls with --ssl-bump for URL path filtering and --allow-host-ports for host services rather than loosening the entry.

references.title: Reject invalid domain allowlist forms and normalize scheme casing
checkDomainSyntax() rejects schemes, paths, user information and ports
Rejected domain forms and case-insensitive protocol prefixes
